events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.90 (model confidence 0.83)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip [F8], so detour kilometres enter the fare directly through the meter and RD-2's metered branch applies: the refund is Σ extra_km of non-exempt off-route segments × this trip's per-km rate [RD-2][F5][F8].

One off-route segment exists: F4, 17:37–17:53, 7.60 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.70 km, adding 4.89 km [F4][F1]. The trace settles there was no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch [F15], so RD-4 gives no exemption and RD-4(b)'s speed bands (F13, F14) are corroboration only [RD-4].

What remains is whether the rider excused that segment. The rider's only message before the segment began is F9 (17:33): "Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way? Just need 2 minutes," which the driver accepted with "Sure" at 17:34 [F9][F10][F11]. That names no place, so RD-3(a)'s naming requirement is not met: the rider agreed to a stop, not to the driver's choice of a far-away 7-Eleven [RD-3(a)]. The double (b) branch applies on its own terms: the rider did not name the place, the driver chose a location with a detour, and nothing in the chat informed the rider beforehand which store was chosen — the statement that he "went to the one I know" appears only in the post-trip driver statement, which is a claim, not consent and not prior notice [F12][RD-3(b)][RD-5][G11]. The stationary record F2 (4 min 10 s at 1.3127, 103.8848, 4918 m from pickup, 5158 m from drop-off, not a pickup or drop-off point) confirms a stop was made off the route [F2].

On the RD-5 reading the ground is the rider asking for a stop on the way, i.e. scope_other: the words cover a brief stop, not an errand to a store the driver selected away from the route, so the segment counts [F9][F10][RD-5]. The driver's own statement naming that he drove to the store he knew and the rider's complaint about a store "far off the route" both place the segment outside anything the rider agreed to [F12][Complaint][RD-5].

Amount: 4.89 km of extra distance is attributed to the unexempt segment [F4]; the trace's worked figure bills 5.47 km × $1.4102/km = $7.71 [F5], and 4.89 km × $1.4102/km = $6.896 ≈ $6.90, so I award the segment's own extra km rather than the larger fare-excess figure, which under RD-2 includes unmatched mileage that is not refundable [F5][RD-2]. The stop itself was only 4 min 10 s [F2] and the waiting fee billed was $1.19 [F6] — the rider does not contest the wait and RydeTAXI may charge meter waiting units, so that item stands [RD-3(c)]. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days but 0 of them route disputes [F18][RD-6], so no account flag.

Safety screen: I read F9, F10, F11, F12 and the complaint for threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks and dangerous-driving allegations; the messages are a stop request, a one-word acceptance and a post-trip explanation, with no hostile or abusive language and no collision or injury alleged [F9][F10][F11][F12] — safety_concern is none [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the trace marks the segment measured, the incident screen failed, and the chat is complete with every message timestamped, so every element my ruling needs is settled [F4][F11][F15].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher of $6.90 to the rider (unexempt detour km × this trip's per-km rate) and record the driver's RD-1 breach.

A partial refund, not no_action and not the full amount.

Under RD-3(b)/RD-5 the agreed scope was a stop 'on the way' only, so the segment's 4.89 extra km [F4] is not exempt.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your dispute about the extra distance on this trip. You asked for a quick stop on the way; the driver agreed, but chose a store well off your route without telling you which one beforehand. That stretch was 4.89 km longer than the best route, so we're refunding $6.90 as a Ryde voucher, added to your account. The wait charge stays, since you asked for the stop and it was brief. No change is needed on your side. The driver's record has been noted for the route choice.

DRIVER: We reviewed the route on this trip. The rider asked for a short stop on the way and you agreed, but you picked a store well off the route and did not say which store beforehand. That added 4.89 km beyond the best route, so we're refunding the rider $6.90 as a Ryde voucher and recording a route breach on your account. The wait charge stays. This is your only route dispute in the last 90 days, so your account is not flagged — but further route breaches could lead to review. No reply needed.

The stationary record F2 (4 min 10 s at 1.3127, 103.8848, 4918 m from pickup, 5158 m from drop-off, not a pickup or drop-off point) confirms a stop was made off the route [F2].

On the RD-5 reading the ground is the rider asking for a stop on the way, i.e. scope_other: the words cover a brief stop, not an errand to a store the driver selected away from the route, so the segment counts [F9][F10][RD-5]. The driver's own statement naming that he drove to the store he knew and the rider's complaint about a store "far off the route" both place the segment outside anything the rider agreed to [F12][Complaint][RD-5].

Amount: 4.89 km of extra distance is attributed to the unexempt segment [F4]; the trace's worked figure bills 5.47 km × $1.4102/km = $7.71 [F5], and 4.89 km × $1.4102/km = $6.896 ≈ $6.90, so I award the segment's own extra km rather than the larger fare-excess figure, which under RD-2 includes unmatched mileage that is not refundable [F5][RD-2]. The stop itself was only 4 min 10 s [F2] and the waiting fee billed was $1.19 [F6] — the rider does not contest the wait and RydeTAXI may charge meter waiting units, so that item stands [RD-3(c)]. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days but 0 of them route disputes [F18][RD-6], so no account flag.

Safety screen: I read F9, F10, F11, F12 and the complaint for threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks and dangerous-driving allegations; the messages are a stop request, a one-word acceptance and a post-trip explanation, with no hostile or abusive language and no collision or injury alleged [F9][F10][F11][F12] — safety_concern is none [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the trace marks the segment measured, the incident screen failed, and the chat is complete with every message timestamped, so every element my ruling needs is settled [F4][F11][F15].

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's position (both briefs request no_action) rests on consent to the detour; the only pre-segment rider message asks for a 7-Eleven stop without naming a place [F9], and the driver's own account of choosing the store he knew appears only in his post-trip statement [F12], which is a claim, not consent or prior notice under RD-5 and G11. RD-3(b) therefore leaves the segment's extra km with the driver.

To the extent the rider's 'no_action' request implies the whole $7.71 fare-excess should be returned, RD-2 refunds only the unexempt segment's own extra km [F4]; the unmatched mileage in the fare-excess figure and the metered waiting units ($1.19, 4 min 10 s) are not refundable under RD-2 / RD-3(c) [F5][F6][F2]. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts.
